reviewDraft.title: Review Draft
reviewDraft.noLlmProfile: Configure an LLM profile in Settings to generate a review draft.
reviewDraft.hallucinationWarning: This is an LLM-generated draft from titles and abstracts only. It may contain inaccuracies, misattributions, or hallucinated claims — verify every citation and factual statement against the source papers before using this text.
reviewDraft.customPromptPlaceholder: You are an academic writing assistant helping a researcher draft a literature review. Write in formal academic style, in Markdown, WITHOUT a top-level heading (the caller adds its own heading). Cite papers inline by title and year in parentheses, not by number. Ground every claim strictly in the material provided — do not invent findings, authors, or numbers that aren't given to you. Match the dominant language of the provided titles/abstracts. Keep each response to roughly 150-350 words.
reviewDraft.customPromptHint: Leave empty to use the default prompt above.
reviewDraft.noDownloadedPapers: No downloaded papers with PDFs yet. Download papers first.

welcome.title: Welcome to Papeer!
welcome.description:
This tool helps you search, review, and download academic papers.
Want a quick tour of the main features?

profiles.title: Switch Between Research Profiles
profiles.description: Use the profile switcher in the header to switch between your research projects. Click '+ Create research' to start a new one.

axes.addDescription:
A topic groups related search queries around one research dimension.

Tip: use 3–5 queries per topic with different phrasings. Add ‘must’ keywords for terms every relevant paper should contain, and ‘boost’ keywords to improve ranking.

You can also import a prepared YAML config via the ⋯ menu.

demo.whySearchDescription: Here you define what to search for. We’ve created a demo research profile and landed on this page — let’s see what was set up.
demo.topicCreatedDescription:
We pre-filled a topic "machine-learning" with:

• 2 search queries (different phrasings)
• 1 required keyword (must be in every paper)
• 3 boost keywords (improve ranking)

In a real research, you’d create your own topics for each dimension of your work.
demo.readyToSearchDescription:
Click Done and the search will start automatically.

It will query Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, CrossRef, and ArXiv in parallel — usually takes about a minute. After that, we’ll move to reviewing the results.

search.title: Run Your Search
search.description:
Searches Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, CrossRef, and ArXiv in parallel, deduplicates results, and scores each paper by keyword relevance (0–10).

Typically takes 1–3 minutes. Watch progress in the log drawer on the right.

papers.filtersDescription: Use search and the Filters button to narrow results: score range, year, citations, tags, and more.
papers.tableDescription: Click a row on the left to see details on the right. Use status segments above to filter by New / Approved / Rejected / Downloaded.
papers.shortcutsDescription:
j / k — navigate up/down
a — approve current paper
r — reject current paper

Works when no text input is focused.

analysis.title: Analysis Dashboard
analysis.description:
Track your review progress here: how many papers found, approved, and downloaded.

Switch to the Citation Graph tab to explore connections between papers.
